summary: The round-10 major is fixed. The gripper now stands on a 25 mm flat foot at y = -r with a true 45 degree rise to y = -6. The print-oriented STL has about 368 mm2 of flat bed contact on two 7 mm edges, and the bed-contact warning is gone. I re-ran the wrist, grip and elbow sweeps in memory at 61 samples each: 0 collisions. Gripper-to-forearm clearance stays 1.5 mm and gripper-to-wrist-servo 0.78 mm at every wrist angle. gripper_fea (5.13 of 13 MPa, hot spot at the jaw root where the stall load enters) and torque_wrist (1.91 of 4.7 kg cm) still pass. The teardrops on the horn, mast, hood and driver holes are present and point up in print orientation, and the DESIGN.md base_fea note and deflections (0.13 / 0.24 mm) now match report.json. All remaining findings are minor. The only new one is that the desk-avoidance rule in the use notes is too loose for the grip servo hanging under the palm.

findings.issue: DESIGN.md 'Use notes' tells the IK to reject poses whose tcp or wrist pivot is below z = 15 mm, assuming the jaws are about 12 mm below the tcp line. The grip MG996R hangs under the palm about 31 mm below the tcp. I checked a pose grid with shoulder/elbow in 20 degree steps and wrist at -75/0/75, keeping only poses that pass the documented rule. At shoulder -20 / elbow 0 / wrist 0 (tcp z = 25 mm) the grip servo's lowest point is at z = -6.4 mm, and at shoulder -60 / elbow 60 it is at -2.9 mm. So the rule as written lets the grip servo case hit the desk. The stall FEA covers the printed parts, but the purchased servo case takes the hit.
findings.fix: In DESIGN.md Use notes, base the desk limit on the lowest point of the gripper and grip servo, not the tcp: reject any pose where the tcp is below about z = 45 mm with the wrist horizontal, or compute the grip servo's bottom corner in the IK and keep it above z = 10 mm.

findings.issue: 11.1 % of the surface still prints on support: the palm underside (11 mm above the bed between the plates) and the fixed jaw. This is documented in DESIGN.md and the docstring, and it is the right trade-off for an on-edge print that keeps the plates' bending stress along the layers.
findings.fix: None required. Optionally chamfer the jaw's underside at 45 degrees to cut its support.

findings.issue: Carried over: upper_arm_stall_fea p99.9 is 13.3 MPa against 16 MPa (margin 1.20), at the elbow servo window frame. This is the thinnest margin on the arm, and the DS32xx tab holes are still UNVERIFIED in the catalog.
findings.fix: Test-fit a real DS3225/DS3218 in a printed yoke_r before printing the rest (already in DESIGN.md Risks).

findings.issue: Resolved by documentation: the engine still warns that base_fea's fixed boxes hold no fastener site, and DESIGN.md now explains that the boxes are the four M4 desk-bolt footprints (plain holes with no printed mate). The setup is correct.
findings.fix: Optional: register the desk holes as a site group so the warning goes away.

findings.issue: Carried over: the yaw lead route ends at the servo origin, inside the MG996R case, instead of at its cable boss.
findings.fix: Engine: end a lead at the servo's cable-boss point.

findings.issue: Carried over: kerf/electrical.py leaves the ATO fuse's cold resistance and the holder lead out of each fused run's loop resistance. The margin is still positive.
findings.fix: Engine: add the fuse and holder lead resistance to each fused run.

findings.issue: Carried over: no 45 degree chamfer under the overhanging side of the floor tie bridge.
findings.fix: Optional: chamfer the underside of the bridge block.

findings.issue: Carried over: 11.4 % of the surface prints on support, because the column is centred on the wider foot.
findings.fix: Optional: set the column flush with one side of the foot.

findings.issue: Carried over and accepted: the Nano, the WAGO splices and the fuse holders sit loose on the desk.
findings.fix: None required; an electronics tray would be tidier.
